input.standard: ASTM E741 (concentration decay, single zone); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure the volume of air V_lab served by scrubber-1-v1 (V = Qe * tau) using the four occupants' CO2 as the source and the scrubber as the pump.

monitoring.reason: Four people breathe the Lab's air while the test raises its CO2; their heart rate is watched for the whole test.

steps.why: Rise: reduced effective flow (0.3 m3/min if linear) so the Lab CO2 climbs from 800 ppm toward a higher equilibrium (about 1900 ppm predicted at 30 min for V=30 m3); hatch held closed.
Decay: full speed (Qe = 1 m3/min), record the decay toward its equilibrium (about 1520 ppm for 4 awake occupants), fit C_eq + (C0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau); hatch held closed.

abort.when: CO2 at or above limits.co2AbortPpm (3200 ppm)
the device refuses a step's command
a monitored person leaves 45-120 bpm, monitoring is lost, or one more person enters the Lab

expected.rise: Lab CO2 rises monotonically from ~800 ppm to ~1700-1950 ppm over step 1 (initial slope ~40 ppm/min, flattening), staying under 2500 ppm, if V is near the 30 m3 default, Qe scales linearly with speed and 4 occupants stay awake at ~0.38 L/min each (1.52 L/min).
expected.decay: After step 2 starts, CO2 falls with tau = V/Qe, about 30 min for V=30 m3, toward ~1520 ppm; the first ~3-10 min is distorted by the scrubber's 3.33 min lag and is excluded from the fit. Fitted tau from rise and from decay should agree within ~20%, and V = 1 m3/min * tau should fall within 10-200 m3.
expected.refutation: Rise and decay taus disagreeing by more than ~20%, a decay curve not exponential, or a rise in Hab-B CO2 (co2-2) while the hatch is closed would show the single-zone / closed-hatch hypotheses fail; a faster-than-expected rise would show fewer/more active occupants or a smaller V; a refused speed command invalidates the step.
expected.record: Lab CO2 every minute, scrubber speed and command acceptance, Hab-B CO2 every minute, heart rates.

hypotheses: The hatch is held closed for the whole test; exchange through the closed hatch (design 3 m3/min ventilation with Hab-B) is not measured and is taken as a hypothesis to be checked against Hab-B CO2, not assumed zero.
The four occupants stay in the Lab and keep a steady awake activity (0.38 L/min each; 0.26-0.45 range).
Effective flow scales linearly with speed: Qe = 1 m3/min at 100 percent (datasheet), 0.3 m3/min at 30 percent.
First guess of V is 30 m3 (the register default), used only to size durations and predictions.

justifications.reason: Never command the only scrubber below 30 percent.
Reduced speed for the rise, at the signed floor.
Full speed, above the 30 percent floor.
Abort at the signed ceiling, below the 3500 ppm elevated level.
Working ceiling below abort; predicted peak ~1900 ppm.
Steps total 55 min, within the 60 min ceiling.
Lower heart-rate bound, equal to the signed minimum and the monitor's default band.
Upper heart-rate bound at the signed maximum.

justifications.reference: tau_rise = V/Qe = 30 m3 / 0.3 m3/min = 100 min (first guess V=30); 30 min gives ~+1100 ppm rise, well above sensor noise, under the CO2 ceiling; a full tau would exceed 60 min total
justifications.reason: Bounded by maxMinutes; rise is several hundred ppm.

justifications.reference: tau_decay = V/Qe = 30 m3 / 1 m3/min = 30 min; 25 min plus 30 min rise = 55 min <= 60
justifications.reason: About one time constant, total within the limit.
